glosses: attraction, charm, fascination, spell (quality of inspiring delight or admiration)

glosses: The tendency to attract.

examples.text: The Moon is held in its orbit by the attraction of the Earth's gravity.

glosses: The feeling of being attracted (to something).

examples.text: I felt a strange attraction towards the place.

When you're well enough off so's you don't have to fret about anything but your heft or your diseases you begin to get queer, I suppose. And the queerer the cure for those ailings the bigger the attraction. A place like the Right Livers' Rest was bound to draw freaks, same as molasses draws flies.

glosses: The feeling of being attracted (to something).
Sexual or romantic desire (especially for a specified individual, kind of person, etc).

examples.text: Murphy struggled with his attraction to men while remaining happily married all his life, daily negotiating the challenges of living in two locations simultaneously. These doublings of desire and emotional attachment left their trace in the multiple doublings within […] the billboard painting he made to signpost the home he created with his wife Sara […]

"I'm asexual," Yazhiisai said, the words spilling out faster than she intended. "I don't experience attraction the way most people do. I'm telling you this because I don't want there to be any surprises."

glosses: An event, location, or business that has a tendency to draw interest from visitors, and in many cases, local residents.

examples.text: The new mall should be a major attraction.
Star Tours is a very cool Disney World attraction.

glosses: The sacrifice of pieces in order to expose the enemy king.
An error in language production that incorrectly extends a feature from one word in a sentence to another, e.g. when a verb agrees with a noun other than its subject.
An object, act or words believed to have magic power (usually carries a positive connotation).

examples.text: a charm against evil
It works like a charm.

The witch, repository of hieratic lore and folk legends and occult arcana, became the distributor of philtres and unguents, electuaries and pastilles, herbs and charms and incantations - directed toward sexual pleasures and amatory satisfactions.

glosses: The ability to persuade, delight or arouse admiration.

examples.text: He had great personal charm.
She tried to win him over with her charms.
[…]the charm of Beauties powerful glance.

Muſick has Charms to ſooth a ſavage Breaſt,
 To ſoften Rocks, or bend a knotted Oak.
Charms ſtrike the ſight, but merit wins the ſoul.
Her coyneſs was conquered by aſſiduity, and at laſt ſhe conſented to reſign the treaſure of her charms to my paſſion.

glosses: A small trinket on a bracelet or chain, etc., traditionally supposed to confer luck upon the wearer.

examples.text: She wears a charm bracelet on her wrist.

glosses: The collective noun for a group of goldfinches.
A quantum number of hadrons determined by the number of charm quarks and antiquarks.

examples.text: In trying to understand the long life of the psi particle, physicists postulated the notion of “charm.” Charm, they say, prevents the “easy” decay of particles and thus prolongs their lifetimes. U particles, Dr. Pert said, may carry the property of charm.

Mesons which combine the charmed quark with the up or down antiquarks are denoted the D mesons. These mesons carry explicit charm (i.e. have a non-zero charm quantum number), just as the K mesons carry strangeness.

glosses: A second-order measure of derivative price sensitivity, expressed as the instantaneous rate of change of delta with respect to time.
An icon providing quick access to a command or setting.

examples.text: Undoubtedly one of the most important pieces to navigating Windows 8, charms are actually not visible until a command to show them is given.

glosses: To seduce, persuade or fascinate someone or something.

examples.text: He charmed her with his dashing tales of his days as a sailor.
[…]they, on thir mirth & dance / Intent, with jocond Muſic charm his ear;

The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the furnishing of that atrocious house.

glosses: To use a magical charm upon; to subdue, control, or summon by incantation or supernatural influence; to ensorcel or exert a magical effect on.

examples.text: After winning three games while wearing the chain, Dan began to think it had been charmed.
Nor no witch-craft charme thee.

glosses: To protect with, or make invulnerable by, spells, charms, or supernatural influences.

examples.text: She led a charmed life.
I, in mine owne woe charm’d, / Could not finde death,[…]

glosses: To make music upon.

examples.text: But ah my corage cooles ere it be warme, / For thy, content vs in thys humble ſhade: / Where no ſuch troublous tydes han vs aſſayde, / Here we our ſlender pipes may ſafely charme.

glosses: To subdue or overcome by some secret power, or by that which gives pleasure; to allay; to soothe.

examples.text: Music the fierceſt griefs can charm, / And fate's ſevereſt rage diſarm: […]

glosses: The mixed sound of many voices, especially of birds or children.

examples.text: […]Free libertie to chaunt our charmes at will:[…]

Sweet is the breath of morn, her riſing ſweet,
 With charm of earlieſt Birds;
The laughter rose like the charm of starlings.

glosses: A flock, group (especially of finches).

examples.text: A charm of finches flew overhead, singing into the vivid afternoon sky.

glosses: The act of bewitching, or enchanting

examples.text: Little disappointed, then, she turned attention to "Chat of the Social World," gossip which exercised potent fascination upon the girl's intelligence.

glosses: The state or condition of being fascinated.

examples.text: To my fascination, the skies turned all kinds of colours.

Sliding down the shaft he lay still, the spear jutting above him its full length, like a horrible stalk growing out of his back.
The girl stared down at him in morbid fascination, until Khemsa took her arm and led her through the gate.

But the compensations are many: changing scenes, long days out of doors, freedom from the bondage of conventional life, and above all, the fascination of living among peoples of primitive simplicity and yet of a civilization so ancient that it makes all that is oldest in the West seem raw and crude and unfinished.

glosses: Something which fascinates.

examples.text: Life after death had always been a great fascination to him.

Though more thoughtful than Madame de Mercœur, yet it asked far more knowledge of society—that wilderness of small intricacies—for her to penetrate into the motives of those who seemed so suddenly struck with her fascination; but she was too clear-headed to be deceived, and set it all down under one general belief in caprice.

glosses: Words or a formula supposed to have magical powers.

examples.text: He cast a spell to cure warts.

glosses: A magical effect or influence induced by an incantation or formula.

examples.text: under a spell
Skies are not so black / Mary took me back / Mary has broken your spell
I believe your love has placed its spell on me

glosses: Speech, discourse.
To put under the influence of a spell; to affect by a spell; to bewitch; to fascinate; to charm.

examples.text: Vnchaine your spirits now with spelling Charmes,
[…] although the Kings Jealousie was thus particular to her, his Affection was as general to others […] Above all, for a time he was much speld with Elianor Talbot […]

1697, John Dryden (translator), Georgics, Book 3 in The Works of Virgil, London: Jacob Tonson, p. 109, lines 444-446,
This, gather’d in the Planetary Hour,
With noxious Weeds, and spell’d with Words of pow’r
Dire Stepdames in the Magick Bowl infuse;

But when, O Wells! thy roses came to me
My sense with their deliciousness was spell’d:

glosses: To write or say the letters that form a word or part of a word.

examples.text: I find it difficult to spell because I'm dyslexic.

glosses: To read (something) as though letter by letter; to peruse slowly or with effort.

examples.text: "He'll do," said Bildad, eyeing me, and then went on spelling away at his book in a mumbling tone quite audible.

glosses: Of letters: to compose (a word).

examples.text: The letters “a”, “n” and “d” spell “and”.
In Esperanto each letter has only one sound, and each sound is represented in only one way. The words are pronounced exactly as spelt, every letter being sounded.

Welcome to the League Aiming to Menace and Overthrow Spies!
You realize that spells “LAMOS”?

glosses: To clarify; to explain in detail.

examples.text: Please spell it out for me.

When we get elected, for instance, we get one of these, and we are pretty much told what is in it, and it is our responsibility to read it and understand it, and if we do not, the Ethics Committee, we can call them any time of day and ask them to spell it out for us[…]

glosses: To indicate that (some event) will occur; typically followed by a single-word noun.

examples.text: This spells trouble.

glosses: To constitute; to measure.

examples.text: the Saxon heptarchy, when seven kings put together did spell but one in effect

glosses: To speak, to declaim.

examples.text: O who can tell / The hidden power of herbes, and might of Magicke spell?

glosses: To tell; to relate; to teach.

examples.text:
1770, Thomas Warton, “Ode on the Approach of Summer” in A Collection of Poems in Four Volumes, London: G. Pearch, Volume 1, p. 278,
As thro’ the caverns dim I wind,
Might I that legend find,
By fairies spelt in mystic rhymes,

glosses: To work in place of (someone).

examples.text: to spell the helmsman

glosses: To rest (someone or something), to give someone or something a rest or break.

examples.text: They spelled the horses and rested in the shade of some trees near a brook.

glosses: To rest from work for a time.
A shift (of work); (rare) a set of workers responsible for a specific turn of labour.
A definite period (of work or other activity).

examples.text: A chap named Eleazir Kendrick and I had chummed in together the summer afore and built a fish-weir and shanty at Setuckit Point, down Orham way. For a spell we done pretty well. Then there came a reg'lar terror of a sou'wester same as you don't get one summer in a thousand, and blowed the shanty flat and ripped about half of the weir poles out of the sand.
I had a job in the great North Woods / Workin' as a cook for a spell / But I never did like it all that much / And one day the ax just fell
Despite his ill-fated spell at Anfield, he received a warm reception from the same Liverpool fans he struggled to win over before being sacked midway through last season.

glosses: An indefinite period of time (usually with a qualifier); by extension, a relatively short distance.

examples.text: Even Mrs. Harker seems to lose sight of her trouble for whole spells. [...] When he had spoken, Mina's long spell of silence made me look at her.

glosses: A period of rest; time off.
A period of illness, or sudden interval of bad spirits, disease etc.
An uninterrupted series of alternate overs bowled by a single bowler.
A splinter, usually of wood; a spelk.

examples.text: To swadle a bowe much about wyth bandes, verye seldome dothe anye good, excepte it be to kepe downe a spel in the backe.

glosses: The wooden bat in the game of trap ball, or knurr and spell.
Qualités aimables, attraits, séduction ou ascendant qu’exercent sur l’imagination les objets qui la frappent vivement et qui produisent sur elle l’admiration, l’enthousiasme.

examples.text: Belle Rowena, répondit de Bracy sur le même ton, c’est à vous, à vos propres charmes, qu’il faut attribuer tout ce que j’ai fait, […].

François se dévoyait auprès des filles publiques, […]. On dit que ces professionnelles ont des charmes secrets, des recettes magiques pour exaspérer la volupté de leurs clients et leur procurer des extases sans pareilles.

glosses: Pouvoir de séduction ; talent de charmer.

examples.text: Son plus grand charme venait d’une physionomie dont le calme trahissait une étonnante profondeur dans l’âme.

Les Liméniennes ont toutes de belles couleurs, […], des yeux noirs d’une expression indéfinissable d’esprit, de fierté et de langueur ; c’est dans cette expression qu’est tout le charme de leur personne.

Un air vieux, languissant et funèbre
qui pour moi seul a des charmes secrets.

glosses: Attraits sexuels d’une fille ou d’une femme.

examples.text: Et cependant les sabots garnis de dentelles découvraient admirablement ses bras nus, la gorge s’encadrait dans le pur corsage aux tulles jaunis, aux rubans passés, qui n’avait serré que bien peu les charmes évanouis de la tante.

glosses: Sentiment délicieux que fait éprouver ce qui intéresse le cœur, ce qui fait naître de douces sensations.

examples.text: Quand on traverse pour la première fois une rivière islandaise, on ne peut se défendre de la crainte; mais on s’accoutume vite à ce genre d’émotion, et l'on finit même par y trouver un certain charme.

examples.text: Par la messe ! je crois que le vieux Lucas de Beaumanoir a bien deviné juste, quand il affirme qu’elle a jeté un charme sur vous.
